prompt: we need a checkout page for our storefront, react + tailwind. shipping address, card entry, order summary on the side

guidance.title: One-page checkout
guidance.guidance: Order summary is visible on desktop (side column) and collapsible-but-present at the top on phones with the total always shown; guest checkout first, account optional; sections in the order contact → shipping → payment → review, each with a visible heading and inline validation on blur plus a focused error summary on submit; address fields use autocomplete attributes and correct input types/IME; the pay button states the amount, is disabled only while processing (with a visible status), and is protected against double submission; trust and cost information (shipping, tax) appears before payment, never as a surprise; progress is saved locally so a reload does not lose entries.
covers: inline validation messages and error recovery
confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

implementation.react: Controlled form with per-field touched state; disable pay while pending and announce with role=status; persist draft in sessionStorage.

guidance.title: Editorial storefront
guidance.guidance: Photography full-bleed, asymmetric editorial grid, text-only navigation, serif or grotesk display with a quiet body, monochrome UI so product colour leads, hairline dividers instead of cards, crossfade transitions, one inline CTA per product. Identity via the grid rhythm, type pairing, and image crop language. Do not default to cream+serif+terracotta.

guidance.title: No card containers (dividers and spacing)
guidance.guidance: Remove nested rounded rectangles; group with whitespace and a heading; use a single hairline between rows; only wrap something in a card when it needs its own boundary for tapping, dragging, or elevation. This is the biggest single lever against generic AI layouts.

guidance.title: Everything operable by keyboard, no traps
guidance.guidance: Tab reaches every control in visual order; composite widgets use arrow keys with a roving tabindex so Tab is not consumed by every cell; Escape closes layers and returns focus to the invoker; nothing traps focus except a modal, and the modal itself must be escapable. Provide a keyboard alternative for every drag interaction.

guidance.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guidance.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: Linear wizard / stepper
guidance.guidance: Show step count and current step, allow going back without data loss, put one primary action per step, validate per step not at the end, and let completed steps be revisited. prompt: add a nurse handoff summary screen to our existing hospital tablet app so the night shift sees what changed

guidance.title: Clinical workstation
guidance.guidance: Patient banner always visible (identity, allergies, alerts) as the focal element, master-detail for patient lists and records, strict status colour language with text and icons (never colour alone), large legible numerics with units, quiet neutral surfaces, confirmation for critical actions with the safe default, interruption-safe autosave. Identity via the banner treatment and status language; restraint is the brand.

guidance.title: Sticky action bar
guidance.guidance: Bottom-fixed on mobile inside the safe area, sticky footer on desktop; content gets bottom padding equal to the bar height; the bar must not obscure a focused field (WCAG 2.4.11) so scroll the field into view above it.

guidance.title: Privacy on shared and public screens
guidance.guidance: Assume onlookers: mask sensitive values by default with an explicit reveal (balances, medication, addresses), gate personal profiles and purchases behind a PIN on shared TVs, keep notifications and previews generic on shared screens, clear the session and screen on idle or sign-out (kiosks, waiting rooms), and never show one user's data while another profile is active. Announce masked values to assistive tech as masked, not as the value.
covers: privacy of on-screen data on shared devices
masking of sensitive values with explicit reveal

guidance.title: Target size by platform
guidance.guidance: Web: ≥24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8), 44×44 recommended for touch. iOS ≥44 pt, Android ≥48 dp, kiosk ≥60 px, desktop pointer ≥24 epx with 4–8 px spacing. Extend the hit area beyond the visual glyph rather than enlarging the icon.

guidance.title: Text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large)
guidance.guidance: Body and label text ≥4.5:1, large text (≥24 px or ≥19 px bold) ≥3:1, AAA target 7:1 for long reading and for TV. Measure with tokens.py contrast, never estimate. Placeholder text is text and must pass.

guidance.title: Saving, saved, autosave, session expiry, and permission-denied states
guidance.guidance: Show saving → saved as a quiet inline status with a timestamp (not a toast per keystroke); autosave drafts and say so; warn before a session expires with a way to extend, and never discard entered data on expiry on a personal device (restore the draft after re-authentication; on shared or public screens clear it instead); permission-denied is a designed state that explains what is missing and who can grant it rather than an empty screen; destructive or irreversible saves confirm once with the safe action as default.
covers: confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

prompt: self order kiosk for a burger place. huge touchscreen in a noisy mall, people queue behind you so it has to be quick

Identity via tile geometry, illustration, and the brand colour field.

guidance.title: Toast / snackbar / banner
guidance.guidance: Toast: bottom (mobile) or bottom-left/top-right (desktop) consistent position, ≥5 s or until dismissed, undo where applicable, live region polite. Banner: inline at the top of the region it concerns, dismissible if non-critical. TV: brief overlay in the safe area that never steals focus.

guidance.guidance: Targets ≥60 px, body text ≥20 px, high contrast for glare, one task per screen, reachable-height controls (ADA reach ranges: interactive elements within 380–1220 mm), idle timeout with countdown that clears the session, attract screen as the hub, audio/visual feedback on every tap, and a visible way to cancel at every step.

covers: current location marked; back restores state

guidance.guidance: Row height from the density token (48–72 dp), whole row tappable with one accessible name, trailing chevron only when it navigates, swipe actions mirrored by a visible menu.

guidance.title: Master–detail (list + detail pane)
guidance.guidance: List pane with selection state that is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys change selection, Enter opens), detail pane that updates in place and announces its title to assistive tech. Persist the selected item across navigation. On narrow widths collapse to a two-screen stack with Back.

guidance.title: Everything operable by keyboard, no traps
guidance.guidance: Tab reaches every control in visual order; composite widgets use arrow keys with a roving tabindex so Tab is not consumed by every cell; Escape closes layers and returns focus to the invoker; nothing traps focus except a modal, and the modal itself must be escapable. Provide a keyboard alternative for every drag interaction.

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guidance.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).

prompt: email triage ui, inbox zero style. list, preview, archive/snooze, keyboard first

guidance.title: Empty / zero state
guidance.guidance: Short heading stating the situation, one sentence of why/what next, one primary action (or none if nothing can be done), optional small meaningful illustration, same layout region as the content it replaces, and on TV a focusable action so focus is never lost.

guidance.title: Mobile list and swipe actions
guidance.guidance: Row ≥48 dp / 44 pt, leading avatar/icon optional, title + secondary line, trailing meta or chevron, dividers or spacing, swipe actions with labelled buttons and a menu equivalent, pull-to-refresh where data is live, sticky section headers for grouped lists, lazy lists with stable keys, selection mode via long press with a visible toolbar.

guidance.title: On-screen keypad / keyboard for kiosks
guidance.guidance: Keys ≥ 64 px with ≥ 16 px gaps, one key = one accessible name ('Hyphen', 'Delete', 'Space'), the keypad is a role=group labelled by the field it edits; the value box is focusable and read back through a polite live region as it changes; a persistent format hint (not a placeholder) is tied to the field with aria-describedby and errors set aria-invalid with a specific message ('Day must be 1–31'); focus never falls to the page body after a tap (re-focus the equivalent key after a re-render); a physical keypad or scanner wedge writes into the same field (human-speed keys fill, Enter continues, bursts are treated as scans); masked entry for PINs with a visible dot per character; in accessible mode the keypad and value sit in the reach zone (lower part of the screen).
covers: inline validation messages and error recovery
masking of sensitive values with explicit reveal

guidance.title: Moderate metadata with a hierarchy
guidance.guidance: Rank facts: title, then the deciding fact (price/status), then supporting facts in a muted style; status via badge + text; align numbers; no icon per fact.

guidance.title: Choosing a visual style before understanding product, user, and platform
guidance.guidance: Order of decisions: task and user → environment and input → density and navigation → layout → components → then type, colour, surface, motion. Visual style is downstream of structure. Record the KNOWN/INFERRED/MISSING ledger before choosing a look.

guidance.title: Desktop: keyboard is a first-class input
guidance.guidance: Document shortcuts in menus and tooltips; F2 edits, Delete deletes with undo, Ctrl+F finds, F6 cycles panes; grids use arrow keys and Ctrl/Shift selection; every dialog has a default and cancel button; access keys shown on Alt (Windows).

guidance.title: Users always know where they are and how to go back

guidance.title: Functional thumbnails
guidance.guidance: Fixed size per context, consistent crop (object-fit cover with a focal point), alt text that is empty when redundant with the adjacent text, lazy-loaded below the fold with intrinsic size set.

guidance.title: Catalog grid
guidance.guidance: Responsive columns from a minimum tile width (auto-fill/minmax), consistent aspect ratio per catalog, text under the image not over it unless contrast is guaranteed, and a filter/sort bar that stays reachable. Lazy-load images with reserved aspect boxes to avoid layout shift.

guidance.title: Non-text contrast 3:1 for controls and focus
guidance.guidance: Any visual that identifies a control or its state needs ≥3:1 against adjacent colours. Hairline dividers at 1.2:1 are fine as decoration but an input whose only boundary is that hairline fails.

guidance.title: First-run: permission priming and feature education without blocking
guidance.guidance: Ask for a permission only at the moment the feature needs it, preceded by a one-screen explanation of the benefit and what happens on refusal (priming), then trigger the system prompt; never chain several permission prompts on launch, and always offer a way to continue without the permission. Feature education is non-blocking: a dismissible coach mark or inline tip anchored to the real control, one at a time, never a modal tour on first launch; it can be replayed from help, is skipped for keyboard/screen-reader users unless it is accessible, and stops after it has been dismissed once. Both respect reduced motion and never cover the primary action.
covers: permission priming before the system prompt

guidance.title: Accessible names for every control and image
guidance.guidance: Visible label for inputs (not placeholder-only), aria-label/accessibilityLabel/contentDescription/AutomationProperties.Name for icon-only controls, alt text for meaningful images and alt="" for decorative ones, link text that makes sense out of context. guidance.title: TV: exactly one visible focus at all times
guidance.guidance: Set initial focus deterministically (first actionable content or Play on detail), restore focus to the previously focused item when returning, keep focus on screen (scroll into view), move focus to a sensible neighbour when the focused item is removed, and never rely on colour tint alone for the focused state.

guidance.title: Photo capture field (take, retake, replace, remove)

guidance.title: Mobile: primary actions in thumb reach

guidance.title: Choosing a visual style before understanding product, user, and platform

prompt: wizard for migrating data into our platform from a competitor. connect, map, preview, run. it takes ages to run

guidance.title: Wizard / stepper
guidance.guidance: Step indicator with names and progress (list semantics, aria-current=step), Back never loses data, one primary action per step, review step before submit, resume support, each step a real page/route on web; TV: full-screen steps with default focus on the primary action.

guidance.title: Photo capture field (take, retake, replace, remove)
guidance.guidance: The field shows the thumbnails as one row of ≥ 96 dp tiles plus an 'Add photo' tile; each thumbnail is a single target that opens a sheet with Retake (camera, replaces in place), Replace from gallery, Remove (confirm only if it is the last required photo); state per photo (uploading, pending sync, failed with retry) is shown on the tile with icon + text; the camera permission is primed before the first capture and refusal leaves a way to continue; capture never loses other field values (persist the draft before opening the camera); images are downscaled for upload and the original is kept until sync succeeds; the field is announced as 'Photos, 2 of 4 added' and each tile as 'Photo 1, retake or remove'.

guidance.title: Linear wizard / stepper
guidance.guidance: Show step count and current step, allow going back without data loss, put one primary action per step, validate per step not at the end, and let completed steps be revisited. guidance.title: Form labels, errors, and recovery

guidance.title: Announce dynamic status changes
guidance.guidance: Use a polite live region (role=status / accessibilityLiveRegion=polite / LiveSetting) with a complete phrase ('12 results for shoes'), assertive only for blocking errors; toasts stay ≥5 s or until dismissed and are also logged somewhere reachable.

guidance.title: Mobile list and swipe actions

guidance.guidance: On open: focus the first meaningful control (or the heading), trap Tab inside, inert the background, label the dialog by its title. On close: return focus to the invoker. Feature education is non-blocking: a dismissible coach mark or inline tip anchored to the real control, one at a time, never a modal tour on first launch; it can be replayed from help, is skipped for keyboard/screen-reader users unless it is accessible, and stops after it has been dismissed once. covers: permission priming before the system prompt

prompt: warehouse KPI wallboard for the shop floor screen. throughput, backlog, late orders. nobody interacts with it

guidance.title: One-page checkout

guidance.title: Grids with row actions are one Tab stop

Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: Hover reveals need a non-hover path
guidance.guidance: Hover-revealed content must also appear on focus and be reachable by touch (persistent affordance, long-press, or an explicit menu). Tooltips: dismissible, hoverable, persistent (WCAG 1.4.13). Never put essential actions only in hover.

prompt: we have four different button styles on the same screen. unify them but dont touch the brand colours

guidance.title: Public kiosk
guidance.guidance: Attract screen → hub of large tiles → linear flows with one giant primary action, ≥60 px targets in the reach zone, ≥20 px text with high contrast for glare, brand colour on header and primary action, filled icons with labels, idle timeout with countdown, cancel always visible, audio/visual feedback. Identity via tile geometry, illustration, and the brand colour field.

guidance.title: Dominant brand colour
guidance.guidance: Brand colour on large surfaces with a verified on-colour text token; a secondary neutral for content areas; do not derive the whole palette by tinting everything with the brand hue. Interactive states need visible deltas on the brand surface.

guidance.title: Focus is the action (TV)
guidance.guidance: No 'button-like' cards with an inner button; the whole card is focusable and selectable. Detail screen: ≤4 actions in one row, first focus on Play/Resume, LEFT/RIGHT between them, DOWN to rails. Long press or a Menu key can open secondary actions. Never require diagonal or multi-key gestures.

guidance.title: Brands that differ only by logo, primary colour, and font
guidance.guidance: Run fingerprint.py compare on the candidate brand systems; a COSMETIC-ONLY verdict fails differentiation. Vary at least two structural axes (navigation model, layout topology, density, surface strategy, image strategy, metadata density, CTA strategy) per brand, then cosmetics.

guidance.title: Target size by platform
guidance.guidance: Web: ≥24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8), 44×44 recommended for touch. iOS ≥44 pt, Android ≥48 dp, kiosk ≥60 px, desktop pointer ≥24 epx with 4–8 px spacing. Extend the hit area beyond the visual glyph rather than enlarging the icon.

guidance.title: Semantic colour tokens, not raw hex in components
guidance.guidance: Three layers: primitive palette → semantic roles (bg.canvas, text.primary, action.primary, border.default, focus.ring, feedback.error…) → component tokens where needed. Every theme (light, dark, high-contrast, each brand) redefines only the semantic layer. Validate with tokens.py validate.

prompt: our SwiftUI onboarding is 9 screens of full bleed gradient with giant text. tone it down, it looks like every other AI app

guidance.title: Setup / progress checklist
guidance.guidance: A persistent checklist with a progress summary ('3 of 6 done'), each item stating outcome, time estimate, and one action; completed items stay visible and collapsed; the list is dismissible once essentials are done and reachable again from help; items deep-link to the exact screen and return to the checklist; never block the product behind it. Announce progress changes to assistive tech; keep it out of the main content's focal position.

guidance.title: Single column, one task
guidance.guidance: Content width capped for reading (~60–75 characters per line), vertical rhythm from the spacing scale, primary action reachable without scrolling on the shortest supported viewport, or sticky at the bottom.

guidance.title: One primary action per screen
guidance.guidance: Exactly one filled button per view, secondaries as outlined/text, destructive actions separated and confirmed, button label is a verb phrase naming the outcome ('Save changes'), disabled only with an explanation nearby.

guidance.title: Mobile: follow the platform navigation grammar
guidance.guidance: iOS: tab bar + navigation stack with large titles where idiomatic, sheets for secondary tasks, swipe back. Android: navigation bar, predictive back, top app bar, modal bottom sheets, up vs back. Cross-platform frameworks still map to these; state deviations as brand decisions.

prompt: clean up the checkout, its 3 columns of stuff and users cant find the pay button

guidance.title: One-page checkout
guidance.guidance: Order summary is visible on desktop (side column) and collapsible-but-present at the top on phones with the total always shown; guest checkout first, account optional; sections in the order contact → shipping → payment → review, each with a visible heading and inline validation on blur plus a focused error summary on submit; address fields use autocomplete attributes and correct input types/IME; the pay button states the amount, is disabled only while processing (with a visible status), and is protected against double submission; trust and cost information (shipping, tax) appears before payment, never as a surprise; progress is saved locally so a reload does not lose entries.

confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

guidance.guidance: Structure first, style second: choose the element for its meaning and restyle it. Data tables use <th scope>; layout tables are forbidden; visually hidden headings are fine for screen readers when the visual design omits them.

guidance.title: Desktop status bar as the persistent feedback surface, with next-error navigation
guidance.guidance: One status bar at the bottom of the window with fixed regions (selection summary, sync/save state with timestamp, error count as a link, active filter) separated by real separators, not spaces; validation for the current row/cell is echoed there in words ('Line 50: Quantity must be greater than 0') and the error count opens a list; F8 / Shift+F8 (or the project's convention) walk to the next and previous error and move focus into the cell; error styling never paints over the value text (tint the cell background and keep ≥ 4.5:1 for the text); announce status changes with LiveSetting/UIA so screen readers hear them; the bar keeps its height at every window width.
covers: inline validation messages and error recovery

covers: applied filters as removable chips with counts

guidance.guidance: Responsive columns from a minimum tile width (auto-fill/minmax), consistent aspect ratio per catalog, text under the image not over it unless contrast is guaranteed, and a filter/sort bar that stays reachable. Lazy-load images with reserved aspect boxes to avoid layout shift.

guidance.title: Search and filters: visible state and instant feedback
guidance.guidance: Applied filters as removable chips with a 'clear all', result count announced, debounced query (≈300 ms) with a loading indicator, empty results suggest next steps, filter state in the URL/route, and on TV a search screen with a system keyboard/voice plus results as rails.

guidance.title: Kiosk: public, hurried, standing users
guidance.guidance: Targets ≥60 px, body text ≥20 px, high contrast for glare, one task per screen, reachable-height controls (ADA reach ranges: interactive elements within 380–1220 mm), idle timeout with countdown that clears the session, attract screen as the hub, audio/visual feedback on every tap, and a visible way to cancel at every step.

guidance.guidance: Enumerate states per screen and per interactive component before implementation and verify each visually; test with long strings, zero items, 10k items, and slow networks.

prompt: the dashboard has 14 KPI tiles and they all look equally important. nobody knows where to look first

guidance.title: KPI / stat tile
guidance.guidance: Label, value with unit and tabular figures, comparison (vs previous period) with sign + arrow + colour, optional sparkline, consistent decimal precision, the most important KPI larger or first, no icon per tile unless it disambiguates, whole tile links to the detail. Avoid the 'four identical cards with big numbers and a gradient' default.

guidance.title: Dashboard grid of modules
guidance.guidance: 12-column responsive grid, modules sized by importance (the primary KPI or chart spans wider), reading order = importance order (top-left first), each module a region with a heading and its own loading/empty/error states. Cards are optional: a divider grid with headings is often clearer than nested boxes.

guidance.title: Flat tiles
guidance.guidance: One surface tone step above canvas, 4–8 px radius, no border unless contrast between tile and canvas is below ~1.2:1, consistent inner padding from the spacing scale.

guidance.title: Chart container and interaction
guidance.guidance: Title that states the question, unit and time range visible, legend as direct labels where possible, tooltip also keyboard-reachable (focusable points or a data table toggle), accessible summary text, consistent palette, responsive (reduce ticks, not data), empty/loading/error states, no animation beyond a single load transition and none on data refresh. Provide the data table or CSV.
covers: chart form chosen from the analytical question
accessible chart summary and table alternative

guidance.title: One clear focal point per screen
guidance.guidance: Decide the screen's job and the one element that serves it; give that element the strongest size/contrast/position; demote everything else by one or two steps; navigation and chrome are quieter than content. On dashboards the focal point is the most important metric or the anomaly, not the page title.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

guidance.title: Cards inside cards, everything in a rounded box
guidance.guidance: Justify each container: does the boundary mean something (tappable object, elevation, grouping that spacing cannot express)? If not, replace with headings, spacing, and hairline dividers. Never nest a card in a card; never wrap a single KPI number in a card just to make a grid.

guidance.title: Product marketing site
guidance.guidance: Structure derived from the buyer's questions (what is it, does it work for me, proof, price), a hero that shows the real product, one display face with character, one accent, one orchestrated motion moment, everything else quiet; no icon-feature grids, no gradient blobs, no testimonial carousel by default. Identity via the hero concept and type; run the anti-template check.

guidance.guidance: Current location marked (aria-current, selected tab, breadcrumb, page title); URL/route reflects state on web and deep-linkable screens; back returns to the previous screen with its scroll and selection; titles match the navigation label that led there.
covers: current location marked; back restores state

guidance.title: Choosing a visual style before understanding product, user, and platform
guidance.guidance: Order of decisions: task and user → environment and input → density and navigation → layout → components → then type, colour, surface, motion. Visual style is downstream of structure. Record the KNOWN/INFERRED/MISSING ledger before choosing a look.

prompt: the hero on our homepage is a stock photo of people high fiving and a headline that says 'empower your workflow'. do better

guidance.title: Landing hero
guidance.guidance: The hero is a specific thesis: show the real product or outcome, one headline that a user could repeat, one primary action (a second only if it is a genuinely different path), proof close by (not a logo wall by default), LCP image optimised, text contrast guaranteed, no autoplay video without a poster and reduced-motion handling. Structure varies by product: a demo, a live widget, a number, a photograph, or a form can be the hero.
covers: hero as a specific thesis with real proof

guidance.title: Hero imagery on landing/brand pages
guidance.guidance: The hero is a thesis about the product: show the actual thing (product, interface, outcome). Reserve aspect box to avoid CLS, serve responsive sources, LCP image preloaded, text contrast guaranteed by placement or scrim, and no autoplay video without a static poster and reduced-motion respect.

guidance.title: Serif display accent
guidance.guidance: Display serif at ≥32 px with tight tracking, paired with a neutral sans body; check the pairing on the real background colour; avoid combining with the cream/terracotta palette unless the brand owns it.

guidance.title: Everything operable by keyboard, no traps
guidance.guidance: Tab reaches every control in visual order; composite widgets use arrow keys with a roving tabindex so Tab is not consumed by every cell; Escape closes layers and returns focus to the invoker; nothing traps focus except a modal, and the modal itself must be escapable. Provide a keyboard alternative for every drag interaction.

guidance.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guidance.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).

guidance.title: Measure, rhythm, and hierarchy by contrast of size and weight
guidance.guidance: 45–75 characters per line for prose; vertical spacing from the spacing scale tied to line height; hierarchy from clear jumps (≥1.25×) in size or weight, not from five near-identical sizes; headings closer to the content below than to the content above.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

prompt: restructure the multi tenant switcher, currently a tiny dropdown in the corner and people work in the wrong tenant all day

guidance.title: Menu / dropdown / context menu
guidance.guidance: Opens on click/Enter/Space and on Shift+F10 / right-click for context menus, arrow keys move, type-ahead, Escape closes and restores focus, items are buttons/links with icons only where meaningful, destructive items separated at the end, disabled items stay visible with a reason, positions within the viewport. Mobile: bottom sheet or platform menu.
covers: menu keyboard semantics and focus return

guidance.title: Semantic colour tokens, not raw hex in components
guidance.guidance: Three layers: primitive palette → semantic roles (bg.canvas, text.primary, action.primary, border.default, focus.ring, feedback.error…) → component tokens where needed. Every theme (light, dark, high-contrast, each brand) redefines only the semantic layer. Validate with tokens.py validate.

guidance.title: Only the happy state was designed
guidance.guidance: Enumerate states per screen and per interactive component before implementation and verify each visually; test with long strings, zero items, 10k items, and slow networks.

guidance.title: Users always know where they are and how to go back
guidance.guidance: Current location marked (aria-current, selected tab, breadcrumb, page title); URL/route reflects state on web and deep-linkable screens; back returns to the previous screen with its scroll and selection; titles match the navigation label that led there.
covers: current location marked; back restores state

prompt: our long report page has a table of 5000 rows rendered all at once and paginated at the same time somehow. sort this out

guidance.title: Data table / grid
guidance.guidance: Sticky header, row height by density token, zebra striping optional (prefer hover/selection highlight), column resize/reorder/visibility persisted, sort indicator with aria-sort, selection checkbox column with header select-all and a count, row actions visible on focus as well as hover, inline edit with Enter/Escape, keyboard grid navigation (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/Down), virtualised rows, loading skeleton rows, empty state inside the table body. Financial tables: see numeric rule.

guidance.title: Table-first working screen
guidance.guidance: Table fills the viewport height with internal scrolling and sticky header, row density selectable, column widths persisted, filters as a row of chips/fields above the table (not a hidden drawer), bulk actions appear in the toolbar on selection. Numeric columns right-aligned with tabular figures. Virtualise beyond a few hundred rows.

guidance.title: List rows
guidance.guidance: Row height from the density token (48–72 dp), whole row tappable with one accessible name, trailing chevron only when it navigates, swipe actions mirrored by a visible menu.

guidance.title: Search field and results
guidance.guidance: Prominent field with type=search, clear button, suggestions as a listbox with keyboard support, result count announced, query in the URL, recent searches, empty-result guidance, debounce. Mobile: full-screen search with the keyboard open and results as a list. TV: a dedicated search screen, system keyboard or voice, results in rails, focus returns to the field on BACK.
covers: TV search with system keyboard or voice

guidance.title: Grids with row actions are one Tab stop
guidance.guidance: Tab enters the grid once and leaves it once; arrow keys move between cells/rows (roving tabindex or a focus manager), Enter/Space activates the focused cell's action, Escape returns from an edited cell to navigation mode; row actions become reachable when the row or actions cell is focused and are also available from a row context/actions menu; a table with 24 rows must never produce 24 Tab stops per action column. Announce the current row/column (aria-rowindex/colindex or the platform's automation properties) and keep a visible focus indicator on the active cell.

guidance.title: Virtualise long lists and tables
guidance.guidance: Windowed rendering with stable row heights or measured heights, keyboard focus preserved when rows unmount (roving focus by key), aria-rowcount/aria-setsize so assistive tech knows the real size, scroll restoration on back navigation. Native: LazyColumn/List/FlatList/VirtualizingStackPanel already virtualise; keep keys stable.

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

prompt: we want the iPad version of our note app to stop looking like a big iPhone. sidebar, multi column, the works

guidance.title: Sidebar / navigation rail
guidance.guidance: Grouped items with group labels, active item with indicator + aria-current, collapsible to icon rail with tooltips and accessible names, keyboard: Tab into the rail once then arrows, collapse state persisted, footer for account/settings, no more than two nesting levels; never a second rail for sub-navigation (use the content header).
covers: rail / sidebar grouping, active indicator, collapse
current location marked; back restores state

guidance.title: Editorial columns
guidance.guidance: Primary column 60–75 characters wide, generous line height, figures can break the measure, headings carry the rhythm. A sticky table of contents on wide screens, none on narrow. Resist a hero banner unless the page is a landing page; an article starts with its title.

guidance.title: On-screen keypad / keyboard for kiosks
guidance.guidance: Keys ≥ 64 px with ≥ 16 px gaps, one key = one accessible name ('Hyphen', 'Delete', 'Space'), the keypad is a role=group labelled by the field it edits; the value box is focusable and read back through a polite live region as it changes; a persistent format hint (not a placeholder) is tied to the field with aria-describedby and errors set aria-invalid with a specific message ('Day must be 1–31'); focus never falls to the page body after a tap (re-focus the equivalent key after a re-render); a physical keypad or scanner wedge writes into the same field (human-speed keys fill, Enter continues, bursts are treated as scans); masked entry for PINs with a visible dot per character; in accessible mode the keypad and value sit in the reach zone (lower part of the screen).
covers: inline validation messages and error recovery
masking of sensitive values with explicit reveal

guidance.title: Mobile: safe areas and system insets
guidance.guidance: Content respects safe-area insets (SwiftUI safeAreaInset / .ignoresSafeArea only for backgrounds, Compose WindowInsets + edge-to-edge, RN SafeAreaView/useSafeAreaInsets, web env(safe-area-inset-*)); bottom actions sit above the home indicator/gesture bar; keyboard (IME) insets push the focused field into view.

guidance.title: Desktop screen shrunk to a phone
guidance.guidance: Re-prioritise for the phone's tasks: fewer things, bigger targets, bottom-anchored actions, list rows instead of tables, sheets instead of side panels, platform navigation grammar.
covers: no scaled desktop layout on TV or phone

guidance.title: Mobile: gestures are shortcuts, not the only way
guidance.guidance: Every gesture action has a visible equivalent (overflow menu, button); swipe actions reveal labelled buttons; avoid horizontal swipes inside horizontally scrolling content; respect the platform back gesture; long press shows a menu, never a hidden critical action.

prompt: tune the visual hierarchy on our support ticket detail. the ticket body should dominate but the metadata sidebar screams louder

guidance.title: Moderate metadata with a hierarchy
guidance.guidance: Rank facts: title, then the deciding fact (price/status), then supporting facts in a muted style; status via badge + text; align numbers; no icon per fact.

guidance.title: Master–detail (list + detail pane)
guidance.guidance: List pane with selection state that is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys change selection, Enter opens), detail pane that updates in place and announces its title to assistive tech. Persist the selected item across navigation. On narrow widths collapse to a two-screen stack with Back.

guidance.title: One primary action per screen
guidance.guidance: Exactly one filled button per view, secondaries as outlined/text, destructive actions separated and confirmed, button label is a verb phrase naming the outcome ('Save changes'), disabled only with an explanation nearby.

guidance.title: Empty / zero state
guidance.guidance: Short heading stating the situation, one sentence of why/what next, one primary action (or none if nothing can be done), optional small meaningful illustration, same layout region as the content it replaces, and on TV a focusable action so focus is never lost.

guidance.title: Oversized display text and 'big number' KPIs everywhere
guidance.guidance: Reserve display sizes for one element per screen; app headings 20–28 px; KPI value 24–32 px with a readable label; hierarchy comes from contrast between roles, not from making everything large. TV is the exception with its own scale.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

guidance.title: Spacing from one scale, grouping by proximity
guidance.guidance: A geometric-ish scale (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64), inside-group spacing smaller than between-group spacing (ratio ≥1.5×), alignment to a grid, consistent inset per container type, optical alignment for icons and text baselines. Inconsistent spacing is the most common 'unprofessional' signal.

prompt: our order status uses only colour dots. red green amber. change it, keep behaviour identical

guidance.title: Inline badges and status chips
guidance.guidance: Pill only for status/category/count; text inside the pill (never colour only); ≤2 per item; consistent colour mapping across the product; not clickable unless it is a filter.

guidance.title: Duotone identity
guidance.guidance: Two hues with defined roles (one for surfaces/identity, one for action/emphasis), neutrals derived from the first hue, feedback colours chosen to avoid both. Test that the pair reads for colour-blind users (deuteranopia simulation) since duotones often pick red/green-adjacent pairs.

guidance.title: Never colour alone
guidance.guidance: Pair colour with text, icon, pattern, weight, or underline. Error fields get an icon and message; chart series get labels or line styles; links in prose get underlines; selected rows get a check or a border, not only a tint.

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: Users always know where they are and how to go back
guidance.guidance: Current location marked (aria-current, selected tab, breadcrumb, page title); URL/route reflects state on web and deep-linkable screens; back returns to the previous screen with its scroll and selection; titles match the navigation label that led there.
covers: current location marked; back restores state

guidance.title: Actions only on hover
guidance.guidance: Show on focus too, keep a visible affordance (overflow menu) for touch, and never on TV.

prompt: the mobile checkout keyboard covers the continue button on small androids. also fields jump when the keyboard opens

guidance.title: One-page checkout
guidance.guidance: Order summary is visible on desktop (side column) and collapsible-but-present at the top on phones with the total always shown; guest checkout first, account optional; sections in the order contact → shipping → payment → review, each with a visible heading and inline validation on blur plus a focused error summary on submit; address fields use autocomplete attributes and correct input types/IME; the pay button states the amount, is disabled only while processing (with a visible status), and is protected against double submission; trust and cost information (shipping, tax) appears before payment, never as a surprise; progress is saved locally so a reload does not lose entries.
covers: inline validation messages and error recovery
confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

guidance.title: Sticky action bar
guidance.guidance: Bottom-fixed on mobile inside the safe area, sticky footer on desktop; content gets bottom padding equal to the bar height; the bar must not obscure a focused field (WCAG 2.4.11) so scroll the field into view above it.

guidance.title: Material tonal palette (Android)
guidance.guidance: Generate the scheme from the brand seed, disable dynamic colour if brand consistency is required, use container/on-container pairs rather than hand-picked hex, and verify TV variants with higher contrast (tv-material3 defaults are dark).

guidance.title: Mobile: keyboard and input types
guidance.guidance: Set keyboard type and autocomplete/textContentType/autofillHints per field, return key action (Next/Done), scroll the focused field above the keyboard, keep the primary action reachable while the keyboard is open (or on the keyboard toolbar), and dismiss on tap outside for non-modal forms.

guidance.title: Target size by platform
guidance.guidance: Web: ≥24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8), 44×44 recommended for touch. iOS ≥44 pt, Android ≥48 dp, kiosk ≥60 px, desktop pointer ≥24 epx with 4–8 px spacing. Extend the hit area beyond the visual glyph rather than enlarging the icon.

guidance.title: Every interactive colour has hover/pressed/focus/disabled/selected
guidance.guidance: Define state tokens per role (action.primary-hover/-pressed, bg.selected, text.disabled), keep label contrast on every state, make disabled visibly weaker but readable (≥3:1 recommended even though exempt), selected ≠ focused ≠ hovered. Dark theme redefines all of them.

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

prompt: redo the layout of our medication administration screen. nurses say they scroll too much and miss the due meds

guidance.title: Pagination vs infinite scroll vs load more
guidance.guidance: Tables and admin lists: numbered pagination with page size and total; feeds: load-more or infinite scroll with scroll restoration and a way to link to items; catalogues: load-more; TV rails: lazy append at the rail end. Pagination is a nav landmark with aria-current on the page.

guidance.title: No card containers (dividers and spacing)
guidance.guidance: Remove nested rounded rectangles; group with whitespace and a heading; use a single hairline between rows; only wrap something in a card when it needs its own boundary for tapping, dragging, or elevation. This is the biggest single lever against generic AI layouts.

guidance.title: Single column, one task
guidance.guidance: Content width capped for reading (~60–75 characters per line), vertical rhythm from the spacing scale, primary action reachable without scrolling on the shortest supported viewport, or sticky at the bottom.

guidance.title: Saving, saved, autosave, session expiry, and permission-denied states
guidance.guidance: Show saving → saved as a quiet inline status with a timestamp (not a toast per keystroke); autosave drafts and say so; warn before a session expires with a way to extend, and never discard entered data on expiry on a personal device (restore the draft after re-authentication; on shared or public screens clear it instead); permission-denied is a designed state that explains what is missing and who can grant it rather than an empty screen; destructive or irreversible saves confirm once with the safe action as default.
covers: confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

guidance.title: Users always know where they are and how to go back
guidance.guidance: Current location marked (aria-current, selected tab, breadcrumb, page title); URL/route reflects state on web and deep-linkable screens; back returns to the previous screen with its scroll and selection; titles match the navigation label that led there.
covers: current location marked; back restores state

guidance.title: A desktop or mobile layout enlarged for TV
guidance.guidance: Rebuild around focus: rails and grids, side/top navigation, one visible focus, 10-foot type scale, safe margins, minimal text entry, transport controls, BACK semantics. Reuse data and business logic, not the layout.
covers: no scaled desktop layout on TV or phone

prompt: our set top box guide grid is cramped, channel logos overlap the time bar. tidy the epg layout

guidance.title: EPG / programme guide
guidance.guidance: See the EPG grid pattern for structure; component specifics: cell shows title + time with ellipsis, minimum cell width so 5-minute programmes stay focusable (with a time label on focus), current programme highlighted and the 'now' line updates every minute, channel column sticky with logo + number, day picker above the grid, focus moves by programme not by pixel, long press or a key opens programme detail with record/remind actions, jump-to-now shortcut, mini preview of the focused channel optional.
covers: pinned channel column and now marker
live channel switching and mini guide

guidance.title: Broadcast guide (TV)
guidance.guidance: Top tabs (Live, Guide, Catch-up, Search), a fast EPG grid with a now-line and channel logos, landscape channel cards with live badges, condensed titles with tabular times, flat tonal surfaces so text stays legible over 200 channels, focus border + scale (no glow needed), mini-player while browsing. Identity via the guide's colour coding of genres and the channel-card treatment.

guidance.title: EPG / program guide grid
guidance.guidance: Two-dimensional virtualisation (channels vertical, time horizontal), sticky channel column and time header, programme cells sized by duration with a minimum width so short programmes stay focusable, current time line always visible, LEFT/RIGHT move within a channel's programmes (not by pixel), UP/DOWN keep the same time slot, long press or a shortcut jumps to now, focused cell shows full title + time in a detail strip rather than truncating inside the cell.
covers: pinned channel column and now marker

guidance.title: Mini player / picture-in-picture state
guidance.guidance: The mini player is a single focusable/tappable region anchored to a corner (TV: bottom-right inside the safe margin, never over the focused rail; mobile: bottom above the tab bar; web: bottom-right) with the title (one line, truncated with a full title on focus), live/progress indicator and exactly two actions (expand, close); on TV, SELECT expands to the full player and BACK from the full player returns to the mini state with focus restored to the element that was focused before; playback state (playing/paused/buffering/error) is shown with an icon plus text, and the audio keeps playing while the UI is navigated; the region is excluded from the rail's D-pad focus loop except through an explicit UP/RIGHT move; never autoplay audio from a mini player on page load on web.

guidance.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guidance.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).

guidance.title: Arbitrary spacing and misaligned edges
guidance.guidance: Snap every value to the spacing scale, align left edges of text across components, use one inset per container type, check icon/text baseline alignment, and equalise gaps in repeated structures. This single fix does more for 'looks professional' than any colour change.

guidance.title: TV: 10-foot typography
guidance.guidance: Body ≥24 sp (Android) / ≥29 pt (tvOS) at 1080p design scale, captions ≥20 sp, titles 32–48, display 57–72; sans with large x-height and open counters; short strings (titles ≤2 lines, synopsis ≤3 lines with expansion); avoid thin weights (<400) and light text on busy imagery; line height ≥1.3.

guidance.title: Measure, rhythm, and hierarchy by contrast of size and weight
guidance.guidance: 45–75 characters per line for prose; vertical spacing from the spacing scale tied to line height; hierarchy from clear jumps (≥1.25×) in size or weight, not from five near-identical sizes; headings closer to the content below than to the content above.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

prompt: clean up our design tokens usage - half the components hardcode hex values

guidance.title: Operational workbench
guidance.guidance: Character comes from precision: a tight 4 px grid, tabular figures, hairline borders with real contrast, one accent used only for selection and primary commands, quiet surfaces, dense but aligned. Identity via a distinctive neutral tint, a characterful monospace for IDs/values, and a consistent status colour language. No hero, no cards-in-cards, no gradients.

guidance.title: Semantic colour tokens, not raw hex in components
guidance.guidance: Three layers: primitive palette → semantic roles (bg.canvas, text.primary, action.primary, border.default, focus.ring, feedback.error…) → component tokens where needed. Every theme (light, dark, high-contrast, each brand) redefines only the semantic layer. Validate with tokens.py validate.

guidance.title: TV: dark-first colour with restrained saturation
guidance.guidance: Dark tinted canvas, text at 87–92% white, accent used for focus and primary only, semantic colours checked at ≥4.5:1 on dark, gradients dithered or avoided (banding on 8-bit panels), test in 'Standard' picture mode on a real panel.

guidance.title: One type scale with named roles
guidance.guidance: Roles display/heading/title/body/label/caption/numeric with size, line height, weight, and letter spacing per role; body ≥16 px web/mobile, 14 desktop, 24 TV; numeric role uses tabular lining figures; headings use tighter line height (1.1–1.25) and body 1.4–1.6. Generate with tokens.py scale and map the roles to the framework's text styles.

guidance.title: Never colour alone
guidance.guidance: Pair colour with text, icon, pattern, weight, or underline. Error fields get an icon and message; chart series get labels or line styles; links in prose get underlines; selected rows get a check or a border, not only a tint.

guidance.title: Dark mode is a redesign of surfaces, not an inversion
guidance.guidance: Elevation = lighter surface (not darker shadow); desaturate accents; text 87/60/38% white steps for primary/secondary/disabled; borders lighten; images may need a slight dim; charts get a dark palette; re-validate every contrast pair.
covers: dark mode as a surface redesign, not inversion

prompt: make the analytics page usable on a phone. right now the chart is 900px wide and just overflows

guidance.title: Chart container and interaction
guidance.guidance: Title that states the question, unit and time range visible, legend as direct labels where possible, tooltip also keyboard-reachable (focusable points or a data table toggle), accessible summary text, consistent palette, responsive (reduce ticks, not data), empty/loading/error states, no animation beyond a single load transition and none on data refresh. Provide the data table or CSV.
covers: chart form chosen from the analytical question
accessible chart summary and table alternative

guidance.title: Mobile: density is bounded by touch
guidance.guidance: Convert tables to list rows with the 2–3 deciding columns, put the rest in a detail screen; filters in a sheet with applied-filter chips; bulk actions via selection mode; numbers stay tabular; row height ≥48 dp. Dense on phone means fewer things, not smaller things.

guidance.title: Mobile: safe areas and system insets
guidance.guidance: Content respects safe-area insets (SwiftUI safeAreaInset / .ignoresSafeArea only for backgrounds, Compose WindowInsets + edge-to-edge, RN SafeAreaView/useSafeAreaInsets, web env(safe-area-inset-*)); bottom actions sit above the home indicator/gesture bar; keyboard (IME) insets push the focused field into view.

guidance.title: One clear focal point per screen
guidance.guidance: Decide the screen's job and the one element that serves it; give that element the strongest size/contrast/position; demote everything else by one or two steps; navigation and chrome are quieter than content. On dashboards the focal point is the most important metric or the anomaly, not the page title.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

guidance.title: Mobile: follow the platform navigation grammar
guidance.guidance: iOS: tab bar + navigation stack with large titles where idiomatic, sheets for secondary tasks, swipe back. Android: navigation bar, predictive back, top app bar, modal bottom sheets, up vs back. Cross-platform frameworks still map to these; state deviations as brand decisions.

guidance.title: Mobile: primary actions in thumb reach
guidance.guidance: Frequent actions in the bottom third; top-left/right for rare actions (back, settings); large phones make top targets a two-handed reach so provide bottom alternatives (bottom search bar, pull-down). Sheets and menus open from the bottom.

prompt: the confirm dialog for deleting a workspace is just an OK button. make deletion of anything in the app feel appropriately serious

guidance.title: Dialog / modal
guidance.guidance: Title as heading, one primary action, safe default for destructive confirmations, focus management per dialog rule, sized to content with max width, scroll inside the body not the page, Escape and close button, backdrop click closes only for non-destructive dialogs. Mobile: bottom sheet or full-screen; TV: full-screen with first focus on the safe action.
covers: confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

guidance.title: Floating action button (Material)
guidance.guidance: One FAB, labelled (extended FAB where space allows), 16 dp from edges, list content padded so the last item is not covered, hides on scroll down if it obscures content. Never use a FAB as a navigation button.

guidance.title: TV: exactly one visible focus at all times
guidance.guidance: Set initial focus deterministically (first actionable content or Play on detail), restore focus to the previously focused item when returning, keep focus on screen (scroll into view), move focus to a sensible neighbour when the focused item is removed, and never rely on colour tint alone for the focused state.
covers: details screen with Play as default focus

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: TV: overscan-safe margins
guidance.guidance: Keep interactive and text content ≥5% from edges: at the 960×540 dp design frame that is 48 dp horizontal and 27 dp vertical (Android guidance: up to 58/28 dp for maximum safety; tvOS: 60 pt sides, 60 pt top/bottom on the 1920×1080 frame). Let rails scroll under the margin so partial cards hint at more content.

guidance.title: TV: 10-foot typography
guidance.guidance: Body ≥24 sp (Android) / ≥29 pt (tvOS) at 1080p design scale, captions ≥20 sp, titles 32–48, display 57–72; sans with large x-height and open counters; short strings (titles ≤2 lines, synopsis ≤3 lines with expansion); avoid thin weights (<400) and light text on busy imagery; line height ≥1.3.

guidance.title: TV: vertical = sections, horizontal = items
guidance.guidance: Every focusable element must be reachable with straight UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT presses; no diagonal reasoning, no hidden hops. Search and settings live at a predictable edge. Grids: LEFT at the first column may enter side navigation, RIGHT at the last column stays. Forms: one field per row, DOWN advances.

prompt: simplify our nav. we have a top bar AND a side rail AND breadcrumbs AND tabs on every page

guidance.title: Sidebar / navigation rail
guidance.guidance: Grouped items with group labels, active item with indicator + aria-current, collapsible to icon rail with tooltips and accessible names, keyboard: Tab into the rail once then arrows, collapse state persisted, footer for account/settings, no more than two nesting levels; never a second rail for sub-navigation (use the content header).
covers: rail / sidebar grouping, active indicator, collapse
current location marked; back restores state

guidance.title: Tabs
guidance.guidance: Tablist with roving tabindex (arrow keys switch, Tab moves into the panel), selected tab marked by more than colour, tab labels short, panel content lazy but state preserved, URL reflects the tab on web; TV: selection on focus with a delay or on SELECT (choose one, be consistent), DOWN enters content.

guidance.title: Filled icons for distance and touch
guidance.guidance: Filled or bold-weight set at ≥24 dp (≥32 dp on TV), always with a visible label in navigation, filled/outline swap allowed only to show selection.

guidance.title: Immersive hero + rails
guidance.guidance: Backdrop crossfades on focus change with a debounce (~300 ms) so scrubbing across a rail doesn't thrash decodes; a scrim gradient guarantees text contrast over any image; the hero text block sits in the safe area with title, one line of metadata, and a short synopsis; the first rail is partially visible so users know to press DOWN. Provide a reduced-motion path with a static backdrop.
covers: media card with one focus target and one status overlay

guidance.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guidance.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.

guidance.title: Web: UI decisions have a JS cost
guidance.guidance: Prefer CSS for hover/transition/scroll-snap, server-render content, island-ise interactive parts, tree-shake icons (import individual icons), lazy-load charts and heavy widgets below the fold, and measure the bundle before and after adding a UI dependency.

prompt: our list rows use hover to reveal the actions so on touch devices nobody can find them

guidance.title: Mobile list and swipe actions
guidance.guidance: Row ≥48 dp / 44 pt, leading avatar/icon optional, title + secondary line, trailing meta or chevron, dividers or spacing, swipe actions with labelled buttons and a menu equivalent, pull-to-refresh where data is live, sticky section headers for grouped lists, lazy lists with stable keys, selection mode via long press with a visible toolbar.

guidance.title: Empty / zero state
guidance.guidance: Short heading stating the situation, one sentence of why/what next, one primary action (or none if nothing can be done), optional small meaningful illustration, same layout region as the content it replaces, and on TV a focusable action so focus is never lost.

guidance.title: List rows
guidance.guidance: Row height from the density token (48–72 dp), whole row tappable with one accessible name, trailing chevron only when it navigates, swipe actions mirrored by a visible menu.

guidance.title: Hover reveals need a non-hover path
guidance.guidance: Hover-revealed content must also appear on focus and be reachable by touch (persistent affordance, long-press, or an explicit menu). Tooltips: dismissible, hoverable, persistent (WCAG 1.4.13). Never put essential actions only in hover.

guidance.title: Actions only on hover
guidance.guidance: Show on focus too, keep a visible affordance (overflow menu) for touch, and never on TV.

guidance.title: Mobile: primary actions in thumb reach
guidance.guidance: Frequent actions in the bottom third; top-left/right for rare actions (back, settings); large phones make top targets a two-handed reach so provide bottom alternatives (bottom search bar, pull-down). Sheets and menus open from the bottom.

prompt: improve the perceived speed of our dashboard. skeletons everywhere but they're the wrong shape and everything shifts on load

guidance.title: Pagination vs infinite scroll vs load more
guidance.guidance: Tables and admin lists: numbered pagination with page size and total; feeds: load-more or infinite scroll with scroll restoration and a way to link to items; catalogues: load-more; TV rails: lazy append at the rail end. Pagination is a nav landmark with aria-current on the page.

guidance.title: Chart container and interaction
guidance.guidance: Title that states the question, unit and time range visible, legend as direct labels where possible, tooltip also keyboard-reachable (focusable points or a data table toggle), accessible summary text, consistent palette, responsive (reduce ticks, not data), empty/loading/error states, no animation beyond a single load transition and none on data refresh. Provide the data table or CSV.
covers: chart form chosen from the analytical question
accessible chart summary and table alternative

guidance.title: Dashboard grid of modules
guidance.guidance: 12-column responsive grid, modules sized by importance (the primary KPI or chart spans wider), reading order = importance order (top-left first), each module a region with a heading and its own loading/empty/error states. guidance.title: Web: reserve space, load fonts and images without shift
guidance.guidance: width/height or aspect-ratio on every media element, font-display: swap with size-adjust or a metric-compatible fallback, preload the display font and LCP image, skeletons match final dimensions, sticky elements don't push content. Target CLS < 0.1, LCP < 2.5 s.

guidance.title: Oversized display text and 'big number' KPIs everywhere
guidance.guidance: Reserve display sizes for one element per screen; app headings 20–28 px; KPI value 24–32 px with a readable label; hierarchy comes from contrast between roles, not from making everything large. TV is the exception with its own scale.

guidance.title: Spacing from one scale, grouping by proximity
guidance.guidance: A geometric-ish scale (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64), inside-group spacing smaller than between-group spacing (ratio ≥1.5×), alignment to a grid, consistent inset per container type, optical alignment for icons and text baselines. guidance.title: Settings screen

reason: no UI vocabulary found; not a UI design task as written

prompt: shrink our design system's card component sprawl - we have Card, PanelCard, InfoCard, MiniCard and BigCard

guidance.title: Windows-native tool (Fluent)
guidance.guidance: NavigationView with grouped items, CommandBar for page commands, 4 epx grid with 32 epx controls, Segoe UI Variable ramp, system accent colour respected with a brand override, Mica backdrop and layered cards with 8/4 px radii, full keyboard/access-key support, light/dark/high-contrast from system resources. Identity via the accent, iconography weight, and pane composition, not by fighting the platform.

guidance.title: No card containers (dividers and spacing)
guidance.guidance: Remove nested rounded rectangles; group with whitespace and a heading; use a single hairline between rows; only wrap something in a card when it needs its own boundary for tapping, dragging, or elevation. This is the biggest single lever against generic AI layouts.

guidance.title: Platform system font
guidance.guidance: Use the platform text styles (Dynamic Type styles, Material type roles, Windows type ramp) so scaling, weights, and optical sizes are correct for free; add brand through colour, layout, and one display accent if needed.

guidance.title: Text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large)
guidance.guidance: Body and label text ≥4.5:1, large text (≥24 px or ≥19 px bold) ≥3:1, AAA target 7:1 for long reading and for TV. Measure with tokens.py contrast, never estimate. Placeholder text is text and must pass.

guidance.title: Semantic colour tokens, not raw hex in components
guidance.guidance: Three layers: primitive palette → semantic roles (bg.canvas, text.primary, action.primary, border.default, focus.ring, feedback.error…) → component tokens where needed. Every theme (light, dark, high-contrast, each brand) redefines only the semantic layer. Validate with tokens.py validate.

guidance.title: One type scale with named roles
guidance.guidance: Roles display/heading/title/body/label/caption/numeric with size, line height, weight, and letter spacing per role; body ≥16 px web/mobile, 14 desktop, 24 TV; numeric role uses tabular lining figures; headings use tighter line height (1.1–1.25) and body 1.4–1.6. Generate with tokens.py scale and map the roles to the framework's text styles.

prompt: the tvOS details screen puts the trailer button first and Play is buried. reorder it

guidance.title: Media details screen, resume playback and watchlist
guidance.guidance: Details: the primary action is Play (or Resume with the remaining time and a Start over alternative) and it takes default focus; metadata is a short scannable block (duration, year, rating, badges as text not colour), synopsis ≤3 lines with an expander, episodes as a rail or list with progress bars and the next unwatched episode preselected; secondary actions (watchlist, trailer, more like this) sit after Play in one row. Resume: a continue-watching row shows progress on each card, resumes at the saved position, and removes finished items; entering a title from the row returns focus to that card. Watchlist: one toggle with a clear on/off state and text label, works from cards and details, and is reflected immediately in the watchlist row. Everything is reachable with D-pad UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT and BACK returns to the row that launched the details.
covers: details screen with Play as default focus

guidance.title: Focus is the action (TV)
guidance.guidance: No 'button-like' cards with an inner button; the whole card is focusable and selectable. Detail screen: ≤4 actions in one row, first focus on Play/Resume, LEFT/RIGHT between them, DOWN to rails. Long press or a Menu key can open secondary actions. Never require diagonal or multi-key gestures.

guidance.title: Focus-revealed metadata (TV)
guidance.guidance: Reveal into reserved space (a fixed detail area above the rails or an expanded card whose height is pre-allocated) so rows never jump; keep the reveal text ≥24 sp; delay the reveal ~150 ms so quick scrubbing does not flash text.

guidance.title: TV: overscan-safe margins
guidance.guidance: Keep interactive and text content ≥5% from edges: at the 960×540 dp design frame that is 48 dp horizontal and 27 dp vertical (Android guidance: up to 58/28 dp for maximum safety; tvOS: 60 pt sides, 60 pt top/bottom on the 1920×1080 frame). Let rails scroll under the margin so partial cards hint at more content.

guidance.title: TV: 10-foot typography
guidance.guidance: Body ≥24 sp (Android) / ≥29 pt (tvOS) at 1080p design scale, captions ≥20 sp, titles 32–48, display 57–72; sans with large x-height and open counters; short strings (titles ≤2 lines, synopsis ≤3 lines with expansion); avoid thin weights (<400) and light text on busy imagery; line height ≥1.3.

guidance.title: TV: vertical = sections, horizontal = items
guidance.guidance: Every focusable element must be reachable with straight UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT presses; no diagonal reasoning, no hidden hops. Search and settings live at a predictable edge. Grids: LEFT at the first column may enter side navigation, RIGHT at the last column stays. Forms: one field per row, DOWN advances.

guidance.guidance: One home screen of large, labelled entry points; each spoke is a linear flow with an obvious way back to the hub. Group entry points by user goal, not by internal system module. On kiosks, the hub also serves as the idle/attract screen and every spoke must time out back to it.

guidance.title: First-run: permission priming and feature education without blocking

guidance.title: Hub and spoke
guidance.guidance: One home screen of large, labelled entry points; each spoke is a linear flow with an obvious way back to the hub. Group entry points by user goal, not by internal system module. On kiosks, the hub also serves as the idle/attract screen and every spoke must time out back to it.

guidance.title: Native accessibility semantics (mobile/desktop)
guidance.guidance: Use platform roles and traits (Compose semantics{role, contentDescription, heading()}, SwiftUI accessibilityLabel/.accessibilityAddTraits, RN accessibilityRole, WinUI/WPF AutomationProperties + AutomationPeer for custom controls); merge descendants so a card is one element; announce async status with live regions/announceForAccessibility. Test with TalkBack/VoiceOver/Narrator, not only by reading code.

guidance.title: Non-text contrast 3:1 for controls and focus
guidance.guidance: Any visual that identifies a control or its state needs ≥3:1 against adjacent colours. Hairline dividers at 1.2:1 are fine as decoration but an input whose only boundary is that hairline fails.

guidance.title: Only the happy state was designed
guidance.guidance: Enumerate states per screen and per interactive component before implementation and verify each visually; test with long strings, zero items, 10k items, and slow networks.

guidance.title: Never colour alone
guidance.guidance: Pair colour with text, icon, pattern, weight, or underline. Error fields get an icon and message; chart series get labels or line styles; links in prose get underlines; selected rows get a check or a border, not only a tint.

guidance.title: Support text scaling and reflow
guidance.guidance: Web: rem units, 200% zoom without loss, reflow at 320 px without horizontal scroll. iOS: Dynamic Type styles, test at AX sizes. Android: sp units, test at 200% font scale. Windows: text scaling 100–225%. Containers grow with text; truncation shows the full text on focus or in a detail.

prompt: the toast that says 'saved' disappears in 1.5s and screen reader users never hear it

guidance.title: Toast / snackbar / banner
guidance.guidance: Toast: bottom (mobile) or bottom-left/top-right (desktop) consistent position, ≥5 s or until dismissed, undo where applicable, live region polite. Banner: inline at the top of the region it concerns, dismissible if non-critical. TV: brief overlay in the safe area that never steals focus.

guidance.title: Saving, saved, autosave, session expiry, and permission-denied states
guidance.guidance: Show saving → saved as a quiet inline status with a timestamp (not a toast per keystroke); autosave drafts and say so; warn before a session expires with a way to extend, and never discard entered data on expiry on a personal device (restore the draft after re-authentication; on shared or public screens clear it instead); permission-denied is a designed state that explains what is missing and who can grant it rather than an empty screen; destructive or irreversible saves confirm once with the safe action as default.
covers: confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions

guidance.guidance: Motion must communicate hierarchy, continuity, feedback, or state; decorative scroll animation slows reading and marks the page as generated. Keep at most one reveal sequence, honour reduced motion, and never animate layout properties.

prompt: look over our Android app with TalkBack on, especially the bottom sheet, and tell me whats broken

guidance.title: Service app (mobile hub-and-spoke)
guidance.guidance: Home as a task hub with large labelled entries and the account balance/status as the single focal element, spokes as linear flows with one primary action each, list rows for history, system type styles for Dynamic Type/font scale, calm neutral palette with one trustworthy accent, illustration only in onboarding/empty states. Identity via the hub's tile geometry, illustration style, and accent.

guidance.title: Photo capture field (take, retake, replace, remove)
guidance.guidance: The field shows the thumbnails as one row of ≥ 96 dp tiles plus an 'Add photo' tile; each thumbnail is a single target that opens a sheet with Retake (camera, replaces in place), Replace from gallery, Remove (confirm only if it is the last required photo); state per photo (uploading, pending sync, failed with retry) is shown on the tile with icon + text; the camera permission is primed before the first capture and refusal leaves a way to continue; capture never loses other field values (persist the draft before opening the camera); images are downscaled for upload and the original is kept until sync succeeds; the field is announced as 'Photos, 2 of 4 added' and each tile as 'Photo 1, retake or remove'.
covers: permission priming before the system prompt

guidance.title: One clear focal point per screen
guidance.guidance: Decide the screen's job and the one element that serves it; give that element the strongest size/contrast/position; demote everything else by one or two steps; navigation and chrome are quieter than content. On dashboards the focal point is the most important metric or the anomaly, not the page title.
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point

guidance.title: Dialog focus management
guidance.guidance: On open: focus the first meaningful control (or the heading), trap Tab inside, inert the background, label the dialog by its title. On close: return focus to the invoker. Escape and the visible close button both close; destructive confirmations put the safe action as default. Use <dialog>/showModal, ContentDialog, .sheet, ModalBottomSheet rather than a div overlay.

Test with TalkBack/VoiceOver/Narrator, not only by reading code.

guidance.title: Text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 large)
guidance.guidance: Body and label text ≥4.5:1, large text (≥24 px or ≥19 px bold) ≥3:1, AAA target 7:1 for long reading and for TV. Measure with tokens.py contrast, never estimate. Placeholder text is text and must pass.

prompt: audit the tap targets in our mobile app, the delete and edit icons are 20px apart and people mis-tap constantly

guidance.title: Filled icons for distance and touch
guidance.guidance: Filled or bold-weight set at ≥24 dp (≥32 dp on TV), always with a visible label in navigation, filled/outline swap allowed only to show selection.

guidance.title: Target size by platform
guidance.guidance: Web: ≥24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8), 44×44 recommended for touch. iOS ≥44 pt, Android ≥48 dp, kiosk ≥60 px, desktop pointer ≥24 epx with 4–8 px spacing. Extend the hit area beyond the visual glyph rather than enlarging the icon.

guidance.title: Mobile: keyboard and input types
guidance.guidance: Set keyboard type and autocomplete/textContentType/autofillHints per field, return key action (Next/Done), scroll the focused field above the keyboard, keep the primary action reachable while the keyboard is open (or on the keyboard toolbar), and dismiss on tap outside for non-modal forms.

guidance.title: Mobile: safe areas and system insets
guidance.guidance: Content respects safe-area insets (SwiftUI safeAreaInset / .ignoresSafeArea only for backgrounds, Compose WindowInsets + edge-to-edge, RN SafeAreaView/useSafeAreaInsets, web env(safe-area-inset-*)); bottom actions sit above the home indicator/gesture bar; keyboard (IME) insets push the focused field into view.

guidance.title: Desktop screen shrunk to a phone
guidance.guidance: Re-prioritise for the phone's tasks: fewer things, bigger targets, bottom-anchored actions, list rows instead of tables, sheets instead of side panels, platform navigation grammar.
covers: no scaled desktop layout on TV or phone

guidance.title: Mobile: gestures are shortcuts, not the only way
guidance.guidance: Every gesture action has a visible equivalent (overflow menu, button); swipe actions reveal labelled buttons; avoid horizontal swipes inside horizontally scrolling content; respect the platform back gesture; long press shows a menu, never a hidden critical action.

prompt: review only, no code changes: is our new admin layout consistent with the rest of the product
reason: not a UI design task: backend work (rest) without a UI design, interaction or accessibility requirement

prompt: our support team says elderly customers cant read the statement page on their phones

guidance.title: Neutral canvas + one accent
guidance.guidance: Neutral scale with a slight brand tint (not pure grey), one accent used for ≤10% of the screen, feedback colours distinct from the accent by hue family (error must not be the accent's hue). Charts get their own categorical palette. Validate every pair with tokens.py.

guidance.title: Mobile list and swipe actions
guidance.guidance: Row ≥48 dp / 44 pt, leading avatar/icon optional, title + secondary line, trailing meta or chevron, dividers or spacing, swipe actions with labelled buttons and a menu equivalent, pull-to-refresh where data is live, sticky section headers for grouped lists, lazy lists with stable keys, selection mode via long press with a visible toolbar.
